newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico denies plans to cut tax incentives.
newsitem.headline: Mexico denies plans to cut tax incentives.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry on Wednesday dismissed talk it intended to eliminate tax incentives in the farming and transport sectors as part of a planned tax reform.
"These reports are totally inaccurate," a Finance Ministry spokesman said.
"We talked about a tax reform at the start of this administration, but there is nothing concrete yet," he added. "We are not contemplating this at the moment."

Mexican financial daily El Economista on Wednesday cited unnamed Finance Ministry officials as saying the government wanted to cut tax breaks, particularly in the farming, forestry and transport sectors.
The resulting savings would be worth the equivalent of 0.5 percent of gross domestic product, it claimed.
The savings would translate into incentives for small and medium-sized businesses, the paper said, without elaborating.
But the spokesman said Finance Ministry officials were due to meet with business leaders in Tijuana on Friday, where they would hear private sector proposals on tax reform.

Mexico has been gradually reforming its tax laws in order to boost receipts while giving some breathing space to companies hard hit by the 1994-95 peso crisis. (( -- Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
